skill_gap.name: shape name unavailable without shapes.md
skill_gap.why: Emit requires `id`, `type` and `name` split from the shape row, but a genre file only gives IDs on its Typical shapes line and words a couple of them in its own table. `set-display` is a typical shape for Entertainment, so the rule 'read shapes.md only when the typical shapes miss' never fires, and the two fields cannot be filled from anything in scope.

notes_for_us: A genre file cannot supply `type` and `name` for its own typical shapes unless it happens to reword them, but `shapes.md` is only reachable when the typical shapes miss. Every emit that takes an unreworded typical shape hits this.

The theme table has no entry for realism or fidelity. 'As realistic as possible' is a rendering constraint, and the instruction to take an off-list theme as written turns it into a theme string that is not a theme.

Step 0 says not to hunt for an option to hold menus, UI or camera behaviour, but `unmatched_options` offers `ui`, `mechanics` and `progression` destinations. It is unclear whether things correctly triaged to `mechanics` should also be logged there, so option counts will differ between lanes.

Entertainment's note splits camera framing (mechanics) from viewpoint placement (layout), which points at `spawn-first-reveal` — but on a SET build there is no avatar and therefore no spawn, and no option means 'where the camera sits'.
Nothing in the handoff can express 'start with the pinball machine and build from there'. A staged or phased scope has no field, so it survives only as prose in `mechanics`.
